u0001.line: National Urban Conclave 2026 (25 Oct 2026) → Bhubaneswar; focus: strengthening urban governance, planning and service delivery towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

u0002.line: RBI's new Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute → inaugurated in Bhubaneswar, Odisha (25 Oct 2026).

u0003.line: IDBI Bank: 60.72% stake → 10955230 Canada Inc. (Fairfax Financial Holdings group); strategic disinvestment worth approx. ₹52,878.08 crore (approved 14 Oct 2026).
u0003.trap: The buyer is 10955230 Canada Inc.; Fairfax Financial Holdings is only the group it belongs to.

u0004.line: India Mobile Congress 2026, tenth edition (8 Oct) → inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi; theme 'Scale Without Boundaries'.

u0005.line: Ministry of Education: five new Centres of Excellence for classical languages → Assamese, Bengali, Marathi, Pali and Prakrit (3 Oct 2026).

u0006.line: RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) extended until 31 December 2026; scheme of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
u0006.hook: RoDTEP letters = Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products.

u0007.line: Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal (Mumbai Port, Maharashtra) → declared India's first plastic-free marine oil terminal (2 Oct 2026).

u0008.line: UPSC completed 100 years (1 Oct 2026); India's first Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926.
u0008.hook: 1926 + 100 = 2026: same date, 1 October, a century apart.
hindi: Union Public Service Commission (संघ लोक सेवा आयोग)

u0009.line: Rabi Marketing Season 2027–28: Cabinet raised MSP of all six mandated rabi crops; wheat ₹2,610/quintal; highest absolute rise → safflower (₹675/quintal).
u0009.trap: Highest absolute increase was for safflower (₹675), not wheat; wheat's figure ₹2,610 is its MSP, not its increase.

u0010.line: Arogya Manthan 2026 (25 Sept) inaugurated by Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda; marked eight years of AB-PMJAY and five years of Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission.
u0010.trap: Eight years = Ayushman Bharat–PM Jan Arogya Yojana; five years = Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. Don't swap.

u0011.line: 72nd National Film Awards → Ekta Nagar, Gujarat (22 Sept 2026); Dadasaheb Phalke Award for the year 2024 → actor Anant Nag.
u0011.trap: The Phalke Award is 'for the year 2024' though given at the 72nd ceremony in 2026.

u0012.line: Semicon India 2026, fifth edition (17 Sept) → inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi in New Delhi; theme 'From Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem'.

u0013.line: 18th BRICS Summit (12–13 Sept 2026) → New Delhi under India's chairmanship; theme: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.
u0013.hook: Theme initials spell B-R-I-C-S: Building, Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, Sustainability.

u0014.line: Fifth Swachh Vayu Survekshan 2026: above ten lakh → Lucknow, Indore, Jabalpur; three–ten lakh → Rourkela; below three lakh → Kalinganagar. Khelo India → Youth Affairs & Sports Ministry.
u0014.hook: UP's capital Lucknow tops the big-city clean-air list.
u0014.trap: Lucknow is first only in the 'more than ten lakh' group; Rourkela and Kalinganagar top the smaller groups.

u0015.line: India's first Department of Military Medicine → Command Hospital, Central Command, Lucknow; inaugurated by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh (29 July 2026).

u0016.line: Ministry of Panchayati Raj launched Samarth Portal for self-reliant panchayats (27 July 2026); 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave panchayats constitutional status.

u0017.line: Sarnath (Varanasi district, UP) → UNESCO World Heritage List at the 48th World Heritage Committee session, Busan, South Korea; India now has 45 sites.
u0017.trap: 48 = session number (Busan); 45 = India's World Heritage Sites after Sarnath. Don't swap.

u0018.line: India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel cell train → between Jind and Sonipat, Haryana (17 July 2026); a hydrogen fuel cell's main by-product is water.

u0019.line: INS Mahendragiri, sixth stealth frigate of Project 17A → commissioned at Visakhapatnam (11 July 2026); Defence Minister Rajnath Singh attended.

u0020.line: 29th National e-Governance Conference (1–2 July 2026) → Jaipur, Rajasthan; theme 'Viksit Bharat 2047: AI-enabled, Data-driven and Secure Digital Governance'; adopted the Jaipur Declaration.
u0020.hook: Held in Jaipur → Jaipur Declaration (venue and declaration share the name).

u0021.line: 12th International Day of Yoga (21 June 2026) → PM Narendra Modi joined the celebrations in Kolkata, West Bengal.
hindi: International Day of Yoga (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय योग दिवस)

u0022.line: Bharat Buildcon 2026 (18–21 June 2026) → organised in New Delhi.

u0023.line: Union Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra Modi approved Phase (2A) of the Ahmedabad Metro Rail Project (10 June 2026).

u0024.line: D. K. Shivakumar sworn in as Chief Minister of Karnataka (3 June 2026), after Siddaramaiah.
u0024.trap: Shivakumar is the new CM; Siddaramaiah was the CM before him.

u0025.line: Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal), Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh → India's 100th Ramsar site (June 2026).
u0025.hook: Ballia's Surha Tal scores the century: Ramsar site number 100.

u0026.line: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare released the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) 2.0 guidelines (May 2026).

u0027.line: Sikkim → declared to have India's first fully paperless judiciary (1 May 2026).

u0028.line: C. Joseph Vijay sworn in as the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu (10 May 2026).

u0029.line: Himanta Biswa Sarma sworn in as Chief Minister of Assam for a second consecutive term (12 May 2026).

u0030.line: New CMs: Kerala → V. D. Satheesan; Bihar → Samrat Choudhary (15 April, after Nitish Kumar); West Bengal → Suvendu Adhikari (9 May, oath by Governor R. N. Ravi).
u0030.trap: R. N. Ravi is the Governor of West Bengal who gave the oath; Suvendu Adhikari is the CM.

u0031.line: Cabinet approved raising Supreme Court strength by 4 judges (May 2026); sanctioned strength becomes 37 judges, excluding the Chief Justice of India.
u0031.trap: 37 is the strength excluding the CJI; the increase itself is only 4.

u0032.line: Union Cabinet approved the Mission for Cotton Productivity (5 May 2026); total outlay ₹5,659.22 crore.

u0033.line: PM Narendra Modi visited Gujarat on 31 March 2026 to open and lay foundation stones for projects; inaugurated Samrat Samprati Museum, Gandhinagar.

u0034.line: BRICS Youth Council Entrepreneurship Working Group Meeting → Indore, Madhya Pradesh (May 2026).

u0035.line: India's first indigenous hydrogen train approved to run on the Jind–Sonipat section (May 2026).

u0036.line: Assam passed the Uniform Civil Code, Assam, Bill, 2026 → third Indian state to do so (May 2026).

u0037.line: Over 90 crore Ayushman Bharat Health Accounts (ABHAs) created under Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (30 May 2026); nearly half of holders are women.

u0038.line: India's first National AI & Digital Water Summit 2026 → Bengaluru (27 May 2026).

u0039.line: Northern Region Agriculture Conference → Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh (24 April 2026), organised by the Union Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

u0040.line: India's first alkaline battery manufacturing facility → commissioned in Jammu (April 2026).

u0041.line: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan paid an official bilateral visit to Sri Lanka (19–20 April 2026).

u0042.line: Femina Miss India 2026 grand finale → KIIT (Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology), Bhubaneswar, Odisha (18 April); Miss India World 2026 → Sadhvi Satish Sail.

u0043.line: President Droupadi Murmu launched the 'Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana' (2 March 2026).

u0044.line: Nitish Kumar resigned from the post of Chief Minister of Bihar (April 2026).

u0045.line: North India's first glass bridge → to be built over Sutlej Lake, Ropar district, Punjab (March 2026).

u0046.line: Union Cabinet approved Regional Connectivity Scheme Modified UDAN (25 March 2026): 100 airports to be developed; total outlay ₹28,840 crore.

u0047.line: PM Narendra Modi became India's longest-serving head of a government (22 March 2026), surpassing Pawan Kumar Chamling (Sikkim CM for 8,930 days).
u0047.trap: The record Modi passed was Pawan Kumar Chamling's (a Sikkim CM), not a former Prime Minister's.

u0048.line: Union Cabinet approved the Small Hydro Power (SHP) Development Scheme (18 March 2026).

u0049.line: Supreme Court, for the first time, allowed withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment for Harish Rana under the passive-euthanasia framework (11 March 2026).
u0049.check: Q114 asks the 'total outlay for this scheme' (₹2,584.60 crore), but this story is about passive euthanasia; it seems to belong to another item (likely the Small Hydro Power scheme).

u0050.line: Census 2027 mascots → Pragati (female enumerator) and Vikas (male enumerator) (5 March 2026).
u0050.hook: Pragati + Vikas = progress + development; Pragati is the female one.
